===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|id=main|:inh|enm:tyme}}
From {{inh|en|enm|tyme}}, {{m|enm|time}}, from {{inh|en|ang|tīma|t=time, period, space of time, season, lifetime, fixed time, favorable time, opportunity}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*tīmō}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*tīmô||time}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*deh₂imō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*deh₂y-||to divide}}. Related to {{m|en|tide}}. Not related to {{noncog|la|tempus}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
* {{cog|sco|tym}}, {{m|sco|tyme||time}}
* {{cog|gsw|Zimen}}, {{m|gsw|Zimmän|Zīmmän|time, time of the year, opportune time, opportunity}}
* {{cog|da|time||hour, lesson}}
* {{cog|ovd|taime||hour}}
* {{cog|fo|tími||hour, lesson, time}}
* {{cog|is|tími||time, season}}
* {{cog|no|time||lesson, hour}}
* {{cog|sv|timma}}, {{m|sv|timme||hour}}.

# {{senseid|en|Q11471}} {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[inevitable]] [[progression]] into the [[future]] with the passing of [[present]] and [[past]] events.
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:time}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Time''' stops for nobody.&nbsp;&nbsp; the ebb and flow of '''time'''}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1937|author=w:Delmore Schwartz|url=http://www.americanpoems.com/poets/Delmore-Schwartz/3856|title=Calmly We Walk Through This April's Day
|passage='''Time''' is the fire in which we burn.}}
#* {{quote-av
|en
|date=May 26, 2023
|author=w:Volodymyr Zelenskyy
|title=Zelenskyy surprises the Johns Hopkins commencement ceremony
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230526060203/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8Fy5fQz9Rs
|publisher=w:MSNBC
|time=0:40
|text=One of the most common truisms on Earth is the advice to value or at least not waste '''time'''. Why has it become so widespread? Every person eventually realizes that '''time''' is the most valuable resource on the planet. Not oil or uranium. Not lithium or anything else, but '''time'''. '''Time'''. The very flow of '''time''' convinces us of this. Some people realize this sooner, and these are the lucky ones. Others realize it too late when they lose someone or something. People cannot avoid it, this is just a matter of '''time'''. But there is a fundamental difference that comes down to the question of '''time'''. The '''time''' of your life is under your control. The '''time''' of life of our force on the front line, the '''time''' of life of all Ukrainians who are forced to live through this terrible Russian aggression unfortunately is subject to many factors that are not all in their control. I do not wish anyone to feel like they are in my shoes, and it's impossible to give a manual on how to go through life so as not to waste '''time'''. However, one piece of advice always works. You have to know exactly why you need today and how you want your tomorrows to look like.}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable}} The feeling of the passage of events and their relative duration, as experienced by an individual.
##: {{ux|en|'''Time''' flies when you're having fun.}}
## {{lb|en|physics|usually|uncountable}} A dimension of [[spacetime]] with the opposite metric signature to [[space]] dimensions; the [[fourth dimension]].
##: {{ux|en|Both science-fiction writers and physicists have written about travel through '''time'''.}}
##* {{RQ:Wells Time Machine||31|So long as I travelled at a high velocity through '''time''', this scarcely mattered; I was, so to speak, attenuated&nbsp;– was slipping like a vapour through the interstices of intervening substances!}}
##* {{quote-book|en|1999|w:Brian Greene|w:[[The Elegant Universe|The Elegant Universe: Superstrings, Hidden Dimensions, and the Quest for the Ultimate Theory]]|publisher=w:W. W. Norton & Company||isbn=9780393338102|204|year_published=2010|We all have a visceral understanding of what it means for the universe to have multiple space dimensions, since we live in a world in which we constantly deal with a plurality — three. But what would it mean to have multiple '''times'''? Would one align with '''time''' as we presently experience it psychologically while the other would somehow be "different"?}}
## {{lb|en|physics|uncountable}} Change associated with the second law of [[thermodynamics]]; the physical and psychological result of increasing [[entropy]].
##: {{ux|en|'''Time''' slows down when you approach the speed of light.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|1992|w:Roger Highfield; w:Peter Coveney|Arrow of Time||179|Given the connection between increasing entropy and the arrow of '''time''', does the Big Crunch mean that '''time''' would run backwards as soon as collapse began?|publisher=w:Ballantine Books|isbn=0449907236}}
##* {{quote-book|en|2012|Robert Zwilling|Natural Sciences and Human Thought|publisher=w:Springer Science+Business Media|isbn=9783642786853||80|Eventually '''time''' would also die because no processes would continue, no light would flow.}}
## {{lb|en|physics|uncountable|reductionist definition}} The property of a system which allows it to have more than one distinct configuration.
##: {{ux|en|An essential definition of '''time''' should entail neither speed nor direction, just change.}}

====Usage notes====
* For the number of occurrences and the ratio of comparison, ''[[once]]'' and ''[[twice]]'' are typically used instead of ''one time'' and ''two times''. ''[[thrice|Thrice]]'' is uncommon in American English and British English but is still common in Asian English, for example in India, Singapore, and Malaysia.<ref>James Lambert, 2012, 'Diachronic stability in Indian English lexis' ''World Englishes'' Vol. 31, issue 1, page 112-127. [https://doi.org/10.1111/weng.12072]</ref>
* {{s|music}} The distinction between ''time'' as tempo ({{senseno|en|tempo}}) and ''time'' as meter ({{senseno|en|meter}}) is relatively modern. The dated expression "march time" refers equally to the tempo of a march as it does to the use of 2/4 or 4/4 meter.
* Ratio usage with comparatives, such as "you earn three times more than me", though common, is strictly illogical. More correctly: "you earn three times as much as me".

====Collocations====
Typical collocations with '''time''' or time expressions.
* [[spend]] - To talk about the length of time of an activity.
: - We '''spent''' a long '''time''' driving along the motorway.
: - I've '''spent''' most of my life working here. (Time expression)
* [[take]] - To talk about the length of time of an activity.
: - It '''took''' a long '''time''' to get to the front of the queue. See also - [[take one's time]]
: - It only '''takes''' five minutes to get to the shop from here. (Time expression)
: - How long does it '''take''' to do that? (Time expression)
* [[waste]] - see [[waste time]]

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[measure]] or [[record]] the time, [[duration]], or rate of something.
#: {{ux|en|I used a stopwatch to '''time''' myself running around the block.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[choose]] when something [[commence]]s or its [[duration]].
#: {{ux|en|The President '''timed''' his speech badly, coinciding with the Super Bowl.}}
#: {{ux|en|The bomb was '''timed''' to explode at 9:20 p.m.}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|
|passage=There is surely no greater wisdom than well to '''time''' the beginnings and onsets of things.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:TIME|title=Your Bedroom Probably Isn't Dark Enough|date=Dec 9 2025|author=Veronique Greenwood
|text=The human body uses light to correctly '''time''' myriad processes, ensuring that liver enzymes are made on schedule, hair cells divide at the right time, and blood pressure stays at a healthy level.
|url=https://time.com/7339298/dark-bedroom-sleep-night-heart-health/}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[keep]] or [[beat]] time; to [[proceed]] or [[move]] in time.
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1861|author=w:John Greenleaf Whittier|title=At Port Royal
|passage=With oar strokes '''timing''' to their song.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To pass time; to [[delay]].
# To [[regulate]] as to time; to [[accompany]], or [[agree with]], in time of [[movement]].
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1717|author=w:Joseph Addison|title=Metamorphoses
|passage=Who overlooked the oars, and '''timed''' the stroke.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Coriolanus|II|ii|passage=He was a thing of blood, whose every motion / Was '''timed''' with dying cries.}}
# To [[measure]], as in [[music]] or [[harmony]].
